newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak police seize radioactive material.
newsitem.headline: Slovak police seize radioactive material.

text.p: Slovak police seized 2.36 kg (5.2 pounds) of radioactive material and arrested four people on charges of illegal trafficking with dangerous substances, a police source said on Wednesday.
The four were arrested in a parking lot near the central Slovak town of Banska Bystrica on Tuesday evening and were all Slovak citizens in a car with Swiss number plates.

A police investigator, who did not wish to be named, told Reuters that the confiscated material was now being analysed. Its origin and final destination were not immediately known but results of the analysis would be available within one week.
"We do not even know whether it was uranium," the police source said.
"The most important fact is that we foiled the sale, and now we can investigate the route how it came here and where it should have gone."

In the last published case of seized radioactive material in Slovakia 18.38 kg (40.5 pounds) of uranium 238 were confiscated in May 1995, as it was being smuggled into Slovakia from neighbouring Hungary.
The police then said neither the seized amount nor its quality were capable of being used in a nuclear weapon.
